children: was in the spotlight on Wednesday as Wall Street reacted to the tech giant's fiscal third-quarter
, which were both better than anticipated.
Shares, however, fell 5% in premarket trading amid investor concerns that the company's earnings may have peaked.
GF Securities analyst Evan Lee, who has a Hold rating on Dell, said the results were "strong," but there is “moderating AI upside.”

Morgan Stanley analyst Erik Woodring raised his price target on Dell to $408 from $403 and reiterated his Equal-weight rating. He added that the company's execution differentiates itself from its competitors, allowing it to take market share and support its margins.

On the recent slide in the stock, Woodring said it leaves more upside in the risk-reward for investors, notable given that the company's board of directors approved the repurchase of an additional $25B in stock.

TD Cowen analyst Krish Sankar lowered his price target on Dell to $325 from $550, citing the recent tech stock slide. Sankar said the results and guidance were strong, but there is a concern that earnings may be peaking, due in part to memory price deflation and financing concerns for neoclouds, both of which may hit demand.
“For the stock to work, we think there needs to be further conviction that CY27 is not peak earnings,” Sankar added. He has a Hold rating on Dell shares.

J.P. Morgan analyst Joseph Cardoso kept his Buy rating on Dell but lowered his price target to $515 from $635 and said the stock has become a “show-me story” for investors amid concerns about margins.
